documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 yo here for yearly physical and cervical screening.

Doing well. Busy summer with her little one. MG stable, no weakness or visual symptoms; neurology visit last November unchanged, next one this fall. Takes pyridostigmine 60 mg three times daily, refills through us.

NKDA. Never smoker, rare alcohol.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: BP normal, other vitals as charted. No ptosis, EOM full. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. No edema.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap sent (last one normal in 2021). Flu shot in October. Labs not needed this year.
- MG: stable, continue current dose.
- Hx gestational HTN: normotensive.

See her next summer.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Date of service: 11/19/2024.

Re: Zoe Tremblay, DOB 4/22/1997

Seen for annual review of myasthenia gravis. She reports no fluctuating weakness, no ptosis, no diplopia and no chewing or swallowing fatigue. Pyridostigmine 60 mg three times a day continues to suit her. NKDA.

On examination she has no ptosis after one minute of upgaze, full eye movements, normal speech, and full strength in neck flexors, deltoids, hip flexors and grip, without decrement on repetition.

Impression: myasthenia gravis, in good control on symptomatic therapy alone.

Recommendations: continue pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. Annual follow-up. We again talked about a future pregnancy; she would like to try in the next year and will contact us before then so we can plan.

documents.title: Mestinon and pregnancy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, we are hoping to try for a second baby later this year. Is it ok to stay on my Mestinon? I took it the whole time last pregnancy but I want to double check. Thanks, Zoe

documents.title: RE: Mestinon and pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Pyridostigmine is generally continued through pregnancy, and stopping it would carry more risk for your MG than staying on it. Please let your neurologist know your plans too, since they will want to coordinate with obstetrics. We can go over the rest of preconception planning at your physical this summer.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 yo F, yearly exam. She plans to start trying for a second pregnancy this fall.

MG: stable, pyridostigmine 60 mg TID, no symptoms. Neurology aware of pregnancy plans per patient.
Prior pregnancy: gestational hypertension, term delivery.
NKDA. Never smoker; drinks only occasionally and will stop when trying.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: vitals as recorded, BP normal. Weight stable. No ptosis. Thyroid normal. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Plan
- Preconception: start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily now. Continue pyridostigmine. Once pregnant, let us know and we will get her to obstetrics early, given her MG and prior gestational hypertension. CBC and TSH today.
- Pap up to date (2024 normal).
- Flu vaccine this fall.

Next physical in a year or sooner with news.

documents.title: Pregnant!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! Two lines on a home test today. My last period started September 4. Feeling fine, a little tired. What should I do next?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Keep taking the prenatal vitamin and pyridostigmine. Our front desk will offer you a short visit this week to confirm and get the obstetrics referral going. Call right away for bleeding or severe cramping.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Positive home test 10/7. LMP 9/4/25, regular cycles, so about 5 weeks today; EDD by dates 6/11/26. Mild fatigue and breast tenderness. No bleeding, no pain. Taking prenatal vitamin since August and pyridostigmine 60 mg TID. No MG symptoms.

O: BP normal, vitals as charted. Well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender. Urine hCG positive in office.

A/P: Intrauterine pregnancy not yet confirmed, about 5 weeks by LMP. Second pregnancy; first had gestational hypertension. Myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine.
- Referral to obstetrics placed, flagged for early high-risk scheduling.
- Continue prenatal vitamin and pyridostigmine.
- She will update neurology this week.
- Nausea and bleeding precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Neurology Letter: Pregnancy Counseling
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Visit of 10/28/2025.

Ms. Tremblay is now about 7 weeks pregnant and came in to plan her myasthenia care through pregnancy and delivery. She remains symptom free on pyridostigmine 60 mg three times a day. Exam today is normal, with no ptosis, diplopia or fatigable weakness.

Recommendations, shared with her and copied to obstetrics and primary care:
1. Continue pyridostigmine 60 mg TID throughout pregnancy and the postpartum period. Breastfeeding is compatible.
2. Several medications can worsen myasthenia and should be avoided or used only after discussion with us, most importantly magnesium sulfate, as well as aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones and macrolides. If magnesium would otherwise be indicated, please call neurology; alternatives exist.
3. Labor itself is usually unaffected, but she should alert the delivery team to her diagnosis on arrival.
4. We will see her postpartum or sooner with any weakness.

Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Routine prenatal visit and vaccination counseling

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics and gynecology practice. Prenatal visit, 11/25/2025.

G2P1, 11 weeks 5 days by LMP of 9/4/2025, EDD 6/11/2026. Seen on referral from primary care.

So far this pregnancy has been uneventful. She is taking her prenatal vitamins every day and has no concerns today. Her main question was about the coming flu season and how best to protect herself and the baby.

PMH: myasthenia gravis, followed by neurology (their counseling letter reviewed). Gestational hypertension in her first pregnancy, which went to term and delivered without problems.
PSH: none.
Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO TID.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother had preeclampsia; a maternal cousin with lupus.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol since conception.

Vitals within normal limits, BP normal. General exam unremarkable.

Plan:
- Inactivated influenza vaccine given today; safe at any point in pregnancy. Discussed that Tdap is recommended between 27 and 36 weeks to pass protection to the newborn; plan for it at the early third-trimester visit.
- Neurology recommendations noted on her chart, including avoidance of magnesium sulfate.
- Routine prenatal care; return in 4 weeks.

cc: primary care
